observations.text: Aloud gives audibility: the inner state of grief, thanksgiving or distress, named by another word of the verse, is voiced so that it is heard.
observations.gives: audibility: the inner state (grief, thanks, distress) made heard

observations.text: Aloud here only carries a public announcement or summons; no inner-being operation is voiced by it.
Aloud, negated, gives withheld voice: the sigh of grief is to be kept inward and not voiced.
observations.gives: withheld voice: the grief kept inward

observations.text: Crying or weeping aloud is itself a purposeful act of the inner being: the voice is raised so as to be heard (by God, by others), and the verse names what it is for or what it brings (heard, answered, mercy asked, restraint overcome).
Quiet here is only the state of a land, a realm, a sea, a place or a weapon (peace after war, calm water); it names no inner-being operation.
Quiet gives a peaceable nature: a calm and gentle disposition of a spirit, a life, a house, or a people, named by another word.
observations.gives: peaceable: calm gentleness in disposition and household

observations.text: Quiet is the inner calm and stillness of a person or God: a chosen or given settledness, or its refusal, that the verse commands, praises, laments the lack of, or promises.
Quiet gives a hush: the calm in which words of the wise are heard better than shouting.
observations.gives: hush: a calm in which words can be heard

observations.text: Quiet gives security: a people or person settled, unthreatened and without fear, named by another word of the verse.
Quiet, negated, gives unrest: the sea of fear that cannot be calm, and the fool's raging so that no calm is left.
observations.gives: unrest: the lack of calm under dread or argument

observations.text: Quieted is here the outward act of one person calming a crowd; it bears on the crowd's inner state but is the speaker's act.
Quieted is the soul's own stilling: 'I have calmed and quieted my soul', like a weaned child, a settled calm after the heart is not lifted up.
Quietly gives the manner of an act: restrained, calm and unobtrusive, in learning, working, looking, waiting on the Lord, or sparing another shame.
observations.gives: manner of an act: restrained, calm and unobtrusive

observations.text: Quietness is itself the settled inner rest and trust: the result of righteousness, the ground of strength, and better than toil and striving.

Silence is here an act upon others or on a state: imposed or removed from outside (good conduct silencing the foolish, God ending the voice of mirth); it enacts a result and is not the person's own inner holding back.
Silence gives dread: the command to be silent comes from fear of naming the Lord in a time of judgment.
observations.gives: dread: speech suppressed by fear of the Lord

observations.text: Silence here is only the absence of sound (the dead, a hush, a command to hush, being talked down) and names no inner-being operation.
Silence is a chosen holding back of speech by the person, in reverence, attention, waiting, grief or submission; the verse names the attitude it expresses, and so silence is the characteristic.
Silence gives awe: the stillness that comes with dread before a presence, in which the voice is heard.
observations.gives: awe: the hush in which the voice was heard

observations.text: Being silent is a person's, or God's, holding back of speech for a reason the verse shows: submission, fear, shame, awe, wisdom, obedience, waiting, or failure to speak up; or the refusal of it (anguish, praise, the watchmen's duty).

Silent is here a command or rebuke to others to be silent: an outward act on another, that bears on their inner state (the cry that will not be hushed, the demon's hold) and not the speaker's own silence.
Silent here is only the absence of voice in a thing or an enforced muteness and names no inner-being operation of the surface.
Uttered here is a pronouncement of God or of Scripture (a thunder, a judgment, a prophecy) and not the voicing of a human inner operation; no inner-being bearing in the surface.

Uttering is the act of bringing out in words or voice what is in the person (a vow, falsehood, rebellion, revilings, words not understood, a loud cry); the verse names what was brought out and so the act is the characteristic.
